# atoms

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*A recoverable filesystem effect engine: the crash-safe substrate*

A change to many files on disk ends finished, undone or halted with evidence kept, never silently half-done, though readers may see it partway. It records its plan before touching anything, so after a crash, a kill or an outside writer the disk alone shows which changes were its own. Domain-neutral, for programs that keep records as files: one host, cooperating processes, certified filesystems.

Authority: `docs/records.md`, `docs/protocol.md`, `docs/durability.md`

## Install

[`verifiably-atoms` on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/verifiably-atoms/):

```sh
pip install verifiably-atoms
```

Linux is complete; macOS fills in capability by capability (the macOS backend is not yet built). Every
mount is probed for the capabilities it supports (`atomic_exchange`,
`noclobber_transfer`, `durable_publish`, …) and only the effects it cannot satisfy are
refused; the crash-certified configurations are the `CERTIFIED_ALLOWLIST`, and every
other tuple fails closed.

## Usage

atoms knows nothing about records, claims or science. Its input is a `TransactionSpec`:
the files a change expects to find and the files it leaves, over five filesystem effects.
Any Python program that keeps its state as files can submit one. It is not ACID: the
files of one change are not made visible to other readers at once, and a reader can see
some of them changed and others not ([docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md)). What the engine guarantees is the
outcome after an interruption: recovery finishes a change that durably committed, undoes
one that had not, and halts without overwriting when the disk holds state it cannot
attribute to itself. A halt can leave a change partly applied; the engine keeps the
evidence and refuses further work on that root until the state is resolved.

[nodes](https://github.com/verifiably/nodes) is the logical side of the family: a corpus
of typed markdown records and the write plans that change it. It decides *what* a write
is and runs each plan through an executor it is handed; its own default executor writes
best-effort. [beliefs](https://github.com/verifiably/beliefs) is where the two meet: its
composition root depends on both and hands nodes an executor that compiles each write
plan into one atoms transaction. Each arrow is a package dependency:

```text
          beliefs
         /       \
        v         v
     nodes       atoms
```

nodes and atoms do not depend on each other, and nodes keeps its TypeScript
implementation, which atoms has none of. A shared or cross-language way to reach the
engine ([docs/durability.md](docs/durability.md)) would answer a consumer that needs one; nodes does not need it to be
useful.

`atoms.coordinator.commands` is the public surface. A project root is registered once;
`run_transaction` then executes a compiled spec against it and converges after a crash
in a fresh process. The engine serializes the processes on one host that go through it;
a sync client such as Dropbox is an outside writer it does not coordinate: where the
disk shows its change, the transaction refuses or halts rather than overwrite it, and
two hosts changing one synced tree is unsupported ([docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md)). Run
this from a directory on a certified ext4 volume (any other configuration fails closed
with `CapabilityUnavailable`, by design):

```python
import hashlib, io, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from atoms.coordinator.commands import register_root, run_transaction
from atoms.core.effects import CreateFileNoClobber
from atoms.core.fingerprint import ABSENT, FileState
from atoms.core.spec import build_spec
from atoms.fs.platform import select_backend
from atoms.fs.volume import StorageProfile

def sha(b): return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
class Payloads:  # a PayloadSource: a fresh stream per call, KeyError when unknown
    def __init__(self, m): self.m = m
    def open(self, digest): return io.BytesIO(self.m[digest])

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=Path.cwd())).resolve()
project, metadata = work / "project", str(work / "project.metadata")
(project / "d").mkdir(parents=True)
backend, storage = select_backend(), StorageProfile(profile_id="flush-honoring-disk.v1")
register_root(backend, str(project), metadata, storage, b"root", ())
body = b"after"; post = FileState(content_hash=sha(body), mode=0o644, byte_len=len(body))
spec = build_spec(consumer_tag="example", intent_digest=sha(b"example intent"),
    initial_surface={"d/f.txt": ABSENT}, final_surface={"d/f.txt": post},
    effects=[CreateFileNoClobber(effect_id="e1", path="d/f.txt", post=post)])
out = run_transaction(backend, str(project), metadata, storage, spec, Payloads({sha(body): body}))
print(out.outcome, (project / "d/f.txt").read_bytes())  # ChainOutcome.COMMITTED b'after'
```

`read_preimage(backend, project, metadata, storage, txid, path, max_bytes=...)` then
returns the bytes a registered path held before a settled transaction.

## Layout

- `python/` — the package: `atoms.core` (the pure model), `atoms.fs` (capability
  backend, volume binding, project approval), `atoms.store` (the SQLite-in-WAL
  metadata store), `atoms.chain` (the tamper-evident project-local history),
  `atoms.coordinator` (lease, admission, preparation, executors, and the public
  `commands`), and `python/tools/certify` (the QEMU crash-certification harness).
- `docs/` — the public reference documentation (`records.md`, `protocol.md`,
  `durability.md`, `development.md`).
